units.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for loading, constructing, and exporting 3D scenes. It reads OBJ, STL, glTF, GLB, COLLADA, 3MF, and FBX files, and writes OBJ, STL, glTF, GLB, 3MF, and COLLADA files through a Scene, Node, and Mesh object graph, with no native runtime or external SDK to install.
It reads .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, and .3mf files using Scene.open() with automatic format detection from the file extension or an explicit FileFormat.
It exports scenes to .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, and .3mf using Scene.save() with format-specific SaveOptions subclasses for coordinate flipping, unit scaling, and compression settings.

It builds and traverses scene graphs using Node.create_child_node(), Node.add_entity(), and Node.child_nodes, where each node carries its own Transform (translation, rotation, scale, and pivots) independent of attached entities or materials.
It creates and edits mesh geometry through Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon(), or by converting parameterized primitives like Box and Sphere using their to_mesh() method.
It assigns LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes, setting diffuse, specular, emissive, and PBR albedo/metallic/roughness color and factor properties directly.
It supports keyframe animation using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and stores skeletal bind-pose data with BonePose and Pose.
It triangulates arbitrary polygons into triangle fans using PolygonBuilder and Geometry.
This example opens a GLTF file and prints the scene hierarchy by walking each node's child nodes starting from the root node.
This example creates a box entity with a Lambert material, adds it as a child node named Crate, and saves the scene as a GLTF file.
The following workflows demonstrate creating scenes, converting meshes, and saving to various formats.
Create a sphere with PBR material and save as STL.
Build a mesh with PBR material and export to text-based glTF.
Generate a triangle mesh and save as ASCII STL.
Convert a Box entity to a mesh and count control points.
Construct a cube mesh and save as uncompressed 3MF.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python provides the aspose.threed.Scene class as the primary entry point for loading and saving 3D scenes, and the aspose.threed.FileFormat class for format detection and options. Scene instances hold a hierarchy of Node objects, each of which can contain Mesh entities and Material instances.

The Scene class supports opening and saving 3D content via Scene.open() and Scene.save(), and provides access to the scene hierarchy through Scene.root_node, Scene.child_nodes, and Scene.sub_scenes; it also manages animation via Scene.animation_clips and Scene.current_animation_clip.

The Mesh class provides control point geometry and polygon construction via Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon, and supports boolean operations through Mesh.do_boolean; Box and Sphere primitives convert to Mesh via their to_mesh() methods.

The shading module exposes Light and Camera classes for scene illumination and view frustum configuration, with Light providing near_plane, far_plane, and aspect properties, and Camera offering near_plane, far_plane, and projection settings.

The animation module provides AnimationClip and AnimationNode classes for keyframe-based animation, where AnimationClip.create_animation_node creates new nodes for animating scene objects, and AnimationNode.find_bind_point locates animation targets.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python reads and writes COLLADA (.dae) files and provides a subset of mesh and curve APIs for geometry manipulation. It supports Python 3.7 and later, with no required third-party dependencies.
COLLADA (.dae) import works, but COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() because the exporter lookup fails before reaching the working ColladaExporter.
FBX (.fbx) import is experimental and lightly verified, while FBX export is not implemented and raises NotImplementedError.
The aspose.threed.render module, including Scene.render() and related classes, raises NotImplementedError — this library does not render scenes to images.
Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction, so an image-backed texture cannot be created, though material color and factor properties work independently.
Mesh Boolean operations (do_boolean, union, difference, intersect) raise NotImplementedError, even though BooleanOperator and BooleanOperand exist as configuration holders.
NURBS curve evaluation and conversion to Mesh are not implemented — NurbsCurve.evaluate() and NurbsSurface.to_mesh() raise NotImplementedError.
A3DObject represents a base object that holds a name and a collection of properties.
AnimationChannel represents a channel that stores keyframe data for a specific animation component.
AnimationClip represents a container for animation data with a defined start and stop time.
AnimationNode represents a node in an animation hierarchy that can hold bind points and sub-animations.
AssetInfo holds metadata about a 3D asset such as author, creation time, and coordinate system.
BindPoint represents a binding point that connects animation channels to a specific property.
BonePose represents the pose of a bone in local or global space.
Box represents a box primitive with configurable dimensions and segmentation.
Camera represents a camera entity used for rendering 3D scenes.
Circle represents a circle primitive defined in 3D space.
Curve represents a curve entity in a 3D scene.
CustomObject represents a user-defined object that extends A3DObject.
Cylinder represents a cylinder primitive with configurable height and segmentation.
Dish represents a dish primitive, a portion of a sphere.
Ellipse represents an ellipse primitive in 3D space.
Entity represents a renderable object in a scene, such as a mesh or geometry.
Extrapolation represents settings for how animation values are extrapolated beyond keyframes.
ExtrapolationType defines how animation values are extrapolated outside the keyframe range.
FileFormat represents supported 3D file formats and provides format detection by extension.
Frustum represents a frustum primitive used for viewing volumes.
Geometry represents a geometric entity that can be rendered in a scene.
GlobalTransform represents a global transformation matrix applied to an object.
INamedObject represents an object that can be identified by a name.
ImageRenderOptions holds settings for rendering a scene to an image.
Interpolation defines the method used to interpolate between keyframes.
KeyFrame represents a single keyframe with a time and value.
KeyframeSequence represents a sequence of keyframes for animation.
Light represents a light entity that illuminates objects in a scene.
LinearExtrusion represents a linear extrusion of a profile along a direction.
Mesh represents a mesh geometry composed of vertices and polygons.
Node represents a transformable object in a scene hierarchy.
Plane represents a plane primitive in 3D space.
PolygonBuilder provides utilities for constructing polygonal meshes.
Pose represents a pose configuration for a node in a scene.
PoseType defines the type of pose, such as bind pose or animation pose.
Primitive represents a basic geometric shape such as a box, cylinder, or sphere.
Property represents a named value that can be attached to an object.
PropertyCollection represents a collection of properties attached to an object.
Scene represents a complete 3D scene containing nodes, entities, and animations.
SceneObject represents an object that belongs to a scene and can be part of the scene hierarchy.
